title: Precomputed study aids for one work in the Library
description: One aid per unit: a plain-language explanation, a situation an officer would recognise, the units it connects to, and — where the unit has one — the misconception it invites, why an examiner asks about it, and a memory hook. Every aid is authored in session against the unit's own text and carries the four-stage authoring record that `data/rules/cards/*.json` carries. NOTHING HERE IS THE LAW. An aid never restates a provision as though it were the text: the reader page renders the provision from the corpus above the aid, and the aid carries `verify: true` unconditionally because it is this project's own writing rather than anything a Ministry published.

unitLabel.description: What one unit is called in this work — Rule, Section or Paragraph.

bilingual.description: Both languages present and non-empty. Equal bilingual footing is a hard rule of this project: a missing Hindi string is a CI failure, never a fallback.

generationMeta.description: The four-stage authoring record docs/AUTHORING.md prescribes, adapted for prose rather than for a keyed question. Stage C here is not a blind answer — an explanation has no key to hide — it is a re-derivation: every claim read back against the unit's own text with nothing else in front of it.

verify.description: grounded=false auto-rejects: an aid that states something the unit does not is exactly what this dataset must not carry.

groundingUnitIds.description: Every unit whose text an assertion in this aid rests on. The first is always the aid's own unit.

unitId.description: A unit id in data/rules/text/<work>.json or data/law/<work>.json — resolved in both directions by tests/library-aids.test.ts.

explanation.description: Two or three plain sentences. What the provision requires, of whom, and the limit on it.

example.description: A situation an officer would recognise. Never a real person, a real file number or a real case.

connects.description: Other unit ids in the same work that an officer reading this one has to hold beside it. May be empty.

verify.description: Always true. An aid is this project's own explanation, not published text, and every surface that renders one says so.
